title: Tenant upgrade failure kill-switch, live-repair playbook and sequenced hotfix
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Multiple customers on Private/VPC reported stalled operator-led upgrades where Helm apply completed but operator reconciliation entered a permanent backoff due to a race between CRD projection and tenant-scoped webhooks. This ticket creates a kill-switch + live-repair playbook and implements a minimal sequenced hotfix to safely abort, heal, and resume upgrades without tenant data loss. Expected outcome: deterministic operator behavior during upgrade failures, documented playbook for SRE/SEs, and a hotfix release that can be applied with minimal blast radius.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy operator v1.9.0 and multiple tenants with tenant-config CRs and custom MutatingWebhookConfiguration referencing controller service.
2) Trigger Helm v3.10.0 upgrade which patches CRD versions and applies a new operator image with new reconcile logic.
3) Simulate control-plane latency (scale down leader, or network delay to kube-apiserver) during post-upgrade webhook registration to create a window where CRDs are partially projected.

4) Observe tenant CRs stuck with status 'reconcileBackoff' and operator pods repeatedly failing webhook admission (timeout) and entering crash loops, leading to Helm upgrade perceived as successful but tenant operations blocked.
root_cause_summary: A race condition between Helm post-upgrade hooks and the operator re-registering admission webhooks caused partial CRD projection; the operator's reconcile path assumed webhook admission success and updated internal tenant schema markers prematurely. When admission failed, the operator would mark tenants in a non-idempotent intermediate state and then backoff exponentially without safe rollback. Additional contribution: some tenants had older external secret controllers that mutate CRs during reconciliation, amplifying state skew.
mitigation: Short-term: provide an emergency CLI 'redwood operator abort-upgrade --namespace <tenant>' that sets operator to maintenance mode, reverts in-memory schema marker, and restarts controller loops. Document manual steps for SREs to remove stale webhook configs and force reconcile. Medium-term: release minimal operator patch that validates webhook readiness before finalizing CRD projection and implements idempotent rollback markers.
proposed_solution: 1) Implement 'upgrade-safeguard' flag in operator that gates CRD projection until all admission webhooks report ready. 2) Add a tenant-scoped tombstone marker when reconcile detects partial projection; this marker is reversible. 3) Add an emergency kill-switch endpoint (authenticated via KMS-backed token) to set operator into live-repair mode which: pauses rolling updates, drains work queues, and runs a staged re-projection + schema-validate step. 4) Ship a 1-line Helm values override for customers to opt-into 'safe-upgrade' mode while we backfill automatic detection.
rollout_plan: Stage A (canary): Build and publish operator v1.9.1-canary to our staging cluster; run end-to-end on 3 internal tenants with simulated apiserver latency.
Stage B (pilot): Offer bundle to 3 paying Private customers that are currently on v1.8.x and have expressed willingness to pilot; coordinate maintenance windows with their SEs.

Stage C (GA): Release operator v1.9.1 with 'upgrade-safeguard' enabled by default and automated migration job that cleans tombstone markers. Provide documented rollback steps and add to release notes.
Emergency hotfix: If customer has blocked upgrade, provide patched chart and step-by-step playbook to apply kill-switch and run live-repair job with remote assistance.
tests: Unit: webhook-ready detector with injected failures (timeout, 500, refused connection)
Integration: helm upgrade flow with webhook registration delay simulation and external secret controller mutation enabled
Chaos: inject leader election pause mid-upgrade and validate tombstone + recovery path
E2E: run blue/green upgrade scenario on staging tenants and verify no transient non-idempotent tenant markers remain
monitoring: Add metric operator.upgrade.progress_state with values [pending, projecting, tombstoned, recovered, failed]
Alert: SEV2 if operator.reconcile.backoff_count > 50 for >15m across any tenant namespace
Dashboards: per-tenant upgrade timeline graph and webhook-registration success rate over time
Audit logs: capture kill-switch invocations with user and token fingerprinting
runbook: 1) Identify affected tenants: query operator status and list namespaces with reconcileBackoff.
2) If immediate customer impact high, run: redwoodctl operator maintenance --set pause=true --namespace <ops>
3) Validate webhook existence: kubectl get mutatingwebhookconfigurations | grep redwood-controller; remove stale entries if safe.
4) Apply live-repair job: helm upgrade --install redwood-repair ./chart --set repair.target=<tenant> --set repair.mode=projection-repair
5) Monitor operator.upgrade.progress_state until 'recovered' then resume maintenance mode with pause=false
6) If repair fails, escalate to SRE oncall and prepare tenant-scoped snapshot rollback using pre-upgrade etcd snapshot (documented per-customer).
comments: 2026-03-14 - Ava Martinez: Triage call summary: three customers affected (ACME corp, Finly, MedData). All reported long-running reconciles post-helm-upgrade. Agreed to freeze further scheduled upgrades until hotfix prepared.
2026-03-14 - Ravi Kapoor: Implemented killing maintenance mode and manual repro steps on staging. Found operator did not validate webhook status prior to marking CRD projection complete.

2026-03-15 - Grace Huang (SRE): Verified live-repair job on staging; repair succeeded for 2/3 simulated tenants; the third failed due to external-mutating controller interfering — added additional preflight check to disable external mutators during repair.
2026-03-15 - Product (Diego Ruiz): Noted customer communications need a short public KB and privately coordinated maintenance windows; approved pilot outreach to ACME and Finly.
